47208-publications-of-the-mississippi-hi.creator: Dunbar Rowland, Ll. D.
47208-publications-of-the-mississippi-hi.description: A book by Dunbar Rowland, Ll. D.. The year 1870 marks an epoch in the history of the South. It witnessed not only the death of Robert E. Lee but the passing also of John Pendleton Kennedy, George Denison Prentice, Augustus Baldwin Longstreet, and William Gilmore Simms. In literature it was not only the end of the old but the beginning of the new, for in 1870 the new movement in Southern literature may be said to have been inaugurated in the work of Irwin Russell.

arxiv-2104-04451.title: Learning constitutive models from microstructural simulations via a non-intrusive reduced basis method
arxiv-2104-04451.creator: Theron Guo, Ondřej Rokoš, Karen Veroy
arxiv-2104-04451.description: Abstract In order to optimally design materials, it is crucial to understand the structure-property relations in the material by analyzing the effect of microstructure parameters on the macroscopic properties. In computational homogenization, the microstructure is thus explicitly modeled inside the macrostructure, leading to a coupled two-scale formulation.

arxiv-2106-14940.title: Phase Transition for a Family of Complex-driven Loewner Hulls
arxiv-2106-14940.creator: Joan Lind, Jeffrey Utley
arxiv-2106-14940.description: Abstract Building on H. Tran’s study of Loewner hulls generated by complex-valued driving functions, which showed the existence of a phase transition [ T ] , we answer the question of whether the phase transition for complex-driven hulls matches the phase transition for real-driven hulls.

arxiv-2111-05465.title: Observation of spontaneous x-ray magnetic circular dichroism in a chiral antiferromagnet
arxiv-2111-05465.creator: Shoya Sakamoto, Tomoya Higo, Masanobu Shiga, Kenta Amemiya, Satoru Nakatsuji, Shinji Miwa
arxiv-2111-05465.description: Abstract X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) signals are usually absent in antiferromagnets. In this letter, we report the observation of spontaneous XMCD spectra originating from the inverse triangular spin structure, or the polarization of the cluster magnetic octupole, in the chiral antiferromagnet Mn 3 Sn thin film.

arxiv-2205-09818.title: A Learning-Based Approach to Approximate Coded Computation
arxiv-2205-09818.creator: Navneet Agrawal, Yuqin Qiu, Matthias Frey, Igor Bjelakovic, Setareh Maghsudi, Slawomir Stanczak, Jingge Zhu
arxiv-2205-09818.description: Abstract Lagrange coded computation (LCC) is essential to solving problems about matrix polynomials in a coded distributed fashion; nevertheless, it can only solve the problems that are representable as matrix polynomials. In this paper, we propose AICC, an AI-aided learning approach that is inspired by LCC but also uses deep neural networks (DNNs).

arxiv-2209-02103.title: Nearest-Neighbor Decompositions of Drawings This research was started at the 4th DACH Workshop on Arrangements and Drawings, February 24–28, 2020, in Malchow, Germany. We thank all participants of the workshops for valuable discussions and for creating a conducive research atmosphere.
arxiv-2209-02103.creator: Jonas Cleve, Nicolas Grelier, Kristin Knorr, Maarten Löffler, Wolfgang Mulzer, Daniel Perz
arxiv-2209-02103.description: Abstract Let 𝒟 \mathcal{D} be a set of straight-line segments in the plane, potentially crossing, and let c c be a positive integer. We denote by P P the union of the endpoints of the straight-line segments of 𝒟 \mathcal{D} and of the intersection points between pairs of segments.

arxiv-2305-01015.title: Collision Detection for Modular Robots – it is easy to cause collisions and hard to avoid them
arxiv-2305-01015.creator: Siddharth Gupta, Marc van Kreveld, Othon Michail, Andreas Padalkin
arxiv-2305-01015.description: Abstract We consider geometric collision-detection problems for modular reconfigurable robots. Assuming the nodes (modules) are connected squares on a grid, we investigate the complexity of deciding whether collisions may occur, or can be avoided, if a set of expansion and contraction operations is executed.

arxiv-2512-03855.title: Fractional Holographic Dark Energy Driven Reconstruction of f ⁡ ( Q ) f(Q) Gravity and its Cosmological Implications
arxiv-2512-03855.creator: Rajdeep Mazumdar, Kalyan Malakar, Kalyan Bhuyan
arxiv-2512-03855.description: Abstract In order to explain the late-time acceleration of the Universe, we present a reconstructed version of the f ⁡ ( Q ) f(Q) gravity theory in this work, which is inspired by the integrating the fractional holographic dark energy with the Hubble horizon as the infrared cutoff.

pmc-10694596.title: Genetic and pharmaceutical targeting of HIF1α allows combo-immunotherapy to boost graft vs. leukemia without exacerbation graft vs. host disease
pmc-10694596.creator: Christopher Bailey, Yuanyi Wei, Jinsong Yan, Dan Huang, Peng Zhang, Chong Qi, Christopher Lazarski, JuanJuan Su, Fei Tang, Chun-shu Wong, Pan Zheng, Yan Liu, Yang Liu, Yin Wang
pmc-10694596.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). SummaryDespite potential impact on the graft vs. leukemia (GVL) effect, immunotherapy targeting CTLA-4 and/or PD-1 has not been successfully combined with bone marrow transplant (BMT) because it exacerbates graft vs. Here, using models of GVHD and leukemia, we demonstrate that targeting hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF1α) via pharmacological or genetic approaches reduces GVHD by inducing PDL1 expression on host tissue while selectively inhibiting PDL1 in leukemia cells to enhance the GVL effect.

pmc-10696204.title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy secondary to deficiency in lysosome-associated membrane protein-2: A case report
pmc-10696204.creator: Ye-Tong Zhao, Xiu-Qun Cao, Xiao-Lin Mu
pmc-10696204.description: BACKGROUNDDanon disease (DD), in which mutations in the X-linked lysosome-associated membrane protein-2 (LAMP-2) gene result in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, is a rare disease, reported primarily in small samples or cases. However, with the development of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging and genetic technology in recent years, the number of reports has increased.

pmc-10709269.title: Impact of preferred surgical modality on surgeon wellness: a survey of workload, physical pain/discomfort, and neuromusculoskeletal disorders
pmc-10709269.creator: Hamid Norasi, M Susan Hallbeck, Enrique F Elli, Matthew K Tollefson, Kristi L Harold, Raymond Pak

The etiopathophysiology of CNS comorbidities in COVID-19, particularly in Long COVID, remains unclear.

pmc-11366627.title: Telemedicine in nutritional management of children with severe neurological impairment: implication for quality of life
pmc-11366627.creator: Veronica Maria Tagi, Francesca Eletti, Jonabell Dolor, Gianvincenzo Zuccotti, Chiara Montanari, Elvira Verduci
pmc-11366627.description: Children with severe neurological impairment (SNI) frequently present feeding problems requiring a close monitoring of their nutritional status. In addition to constant clinical monitoring of body composition and nutritional indexes in these patients, frequent reports of dietary intake and weight gain variations are useful to ensure proper nutritional management.

We analyzed the metabolic activity of Treponema phagedenis and Treponema pedis using gas chromatography–mass spectrometry for organic acids (OAs), amino acids (AAs), and fatty acids (FAs), and high-performance liquid chromatography for short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs). pmc-11592033.title: Harnessing Brain Plasticity: The Therapeutic Power of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) and Theta Burst Stimulation (TBS) in Neurotransmitter Modulation, Receptor Dynamics, and Neuroimaging for Neurological Innovations
pmc-11592033.creator: Minoo Sharbafshaaer, Giovanni Cirillo, Fabrizio Esposito, Gioacchino Tedeschi, Francesca Trojsi, Masaru Tanaka, Simone Battaglia, Donato Liloia
pmc-11592033.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) methods have become exciting techniques for altering brain activity and improving synaptic plasticity, earning recognition as valuable non-medicine treatments for a wide range of neurological disorders. Among these methods, repetitive TMS (rTMS) and theta-burst stimulation (TBS) show significant promise in improving outcomes for adults with complex neurological and neurodegenerative conditions, such as Alzheimer’s disease, stroke, Parkinson’s disease, etc.

pmc-11612317.title: Research on the fatigue performance of continuous beam bridges with vibration-mixed steel fiber-reinforced concrete
pmc-11612317.creator: Zhongyuan Xiao, Jiangfei Wang, Liang Huang, Jianguo Xu, Qi Zhou, Lei Kou, Wanshuai Qi, Jiandong Wei
pmc-11612317.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). To address the fatigue damage issues in continuous beam bridges under vehicle loads, a method using vibration-mixed steel fiber-reinforced concrete to improve critical vulnerable areas of the bridge is proposed, thereby enhancing the bridge’s fatigue resistance. Fatigue performance and micro electron microscopy tests were designed for vibration-mixed steel fiber-reinforced concrete, analyzing its damage conditions and microstructural changes under 0 to 2 million cyclic loads, and the key mechanical parameters of the concrete were determined.

pmc-12836897.title: Utilization of psychotropic medications in individuals with autism spectrum disorder
pmc-12836897.creator: Paula A Jaimes-Buitron, Leslie Neely, Melissa Dziuk Svoboda, Gretchen Gemeinhardt, Carolina Vivas-Valencia
pmc-12836897.description: BackgroundSecond-generation antipsychotics (SGAs), specifically aripiprazole and risperidone, and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), are psychotropic medications commonly prescribed to individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). However, it is unclear how often individuals with ASD initiate with SGAs, how frequently they switch medications, and how utilization has changed over time.

pmc-13175630.creator: Matteo Anselmino, Stefano Bianchi, Raffele De Lucia, Claudio Tondo, Saverio Iacopino, Francesco Solimene, Antonio Rossillo, Matteo Bertini, Sakis Themistoclakis, Ilaria Meynet, Maurizio Russo, Antonio Dello Russo, Gianluca Zingarini, Stefano Bandino, Mario Volpicelli, Pietro Rossi, Lorenzo Bianchini
pmc-13175630.description: BackgroundDespite being the most effective option for maintaining sinus rhythm, atrial fibrillation (AF) catheter ablation reaches few patients. For this reason, identifying candidates with the highest likelihood of success or individualizing counselling to a specific patient to improve procedural outcome could enhance clinical benefits and cost-effectiveness.

pmc-13294894.title: XPS Analysis of Co–Ni Alloy Passive Layers: Computational Peak-on-Satellite Analysis of 2p Core Levels Reveals the Influence of the Co/Ni Ratio on Oxide Chemistry and Structure
pmc-13294894.creator: Barbara Laïk, Morgane Richet, Nicolas Emery, Loïc Perrière, Yvan Cotrebil, Vincent Russier, Ivan Guillot, Pierre Dubot
pmc-13294894.description: Thin native oxide films spontaneously formed on a series of cobalt–nickel alloys with varying cobalt concentrations were investigated using X-ray photoemission spectroscopy (XPS). Combining XPS with sequential ion abrasion allowed identification of the various oxides and hydroxides present within the passive layers, depending on their depth in the films, which do not exceed 5 nm.

pmc-13531843.title: Physical interactions within the SIR heterochromatin complex potentiate inter-subunit communication and gene repression
pmc-13531843.creator: Jenna Kotz, E.J. Martz, Maya Nelson, Nicole Savoie, Lauren Schmitt, Jordan States, Nathan Holton, Danielle Guillen, Vignesh Kasinath, Kirk Hansen, Aaron M. Johnson
pmc-13531843.description: SUMMARYThe Saccharomyces cerevisiae silent information regulator (SIR) complex performs all core heterochromatin functions. It first drives histone deacetylation in an iterative, spreading manner, then stably incorporates with nucleosomes to compact and epigenetically repress the chromatin. How this switch between dynamic spreading and stable compaction occurs has remained poorly understood, partly due to limited structural data on the intact complex.

pmc-13555737.title: Neoehrlichiosis Causing Hemolytic Anemia in Patients Treated with Rituximab, Norway, 2024–2025
pmc-13555737.creator: Martin Paulson, Christine Wennerås, Hanne Quarsten, Kristine K. Berg, Anders L. Drivenes, Magnus Moksnes, Tor Henrik A. Tvedt
pmc-13555737.description: Neoehrlichiosis is caused by infection with the tickborne intracellular bacterium Neoehrlichia mikurensis. We describe 3 cases of direct antiglobulin test–negative hemolytic anemia in rituximab-treated patients infected with tickborne N. mikurensis bacteria in Norway during 2024–2025. All 3 patients had splenomegaly and night sweats.

pmc-13656720.title: Left ventricular pseudoaneurysm rupture following prosthesis infective endocarditis after closure of ventricular septal rupture
pmc-13656720.creator: Yu-san Chien, Tin-ann Chen, Chih-Wei Ten, Wei-Li Hung, Kang-Hong Hsu
pmc-13656720.description: BackgroundLeft ventricular pseudoaneurysm (LVP) is a rare but life-threatening complication of myocardial infarction or cardiac surgery, typically arising within the first few years after ventricular septal rupture (VSR) repair. Delayed rupture associated with prosthetic infection is extremely uncommon and carries high mortality.

pmc-13700441.title: Workplace and personal predictors of well-being in the broader maternity and neonatal workforce during COVID-19: evidence from a multicentre survey
pmc-13700441.creator: Alexander J. Lindgren, Leonie Callaway, Kylie Burke, Elizabeth Ryan, Lisa McKeown, Alka Kothari
pmc-13700441.description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic placed unprecedented pressures on maternity and neonatal services, disrupting models of care and amplifying existing stressors for healthcare staff. While much of the literature has focused on doctors and midwives, less is known about the emotional well-being of the broader multidisciplinary maternity and neonatal workforce, including neonatal nurses, sonographers, allied health, and administrative staff.
